newsitem.title: UK: UK shares seen mixed to lower, focus on results.
newsitem.headline: UK shares seen mixed to lower, focus on results.

text.p: ** UK shares seen opening mixed to weaker, with a
focus on corporate results. Sterling strength,
interest rate concerns loom ahead of BoE meeting.
** NatWest H1 pretax profit from continuing operations
775 million stg. BAA Q1 pretax profits 136 million stg.
UK's leading blue chip shares were expected to remain stagnant at the open on Tuesday ahead of a key two-day interest rate policy meeting beginning on Tuesday, dealers said.
"I'm afraid that the uncertainty about interest rates will keep volumes low and markets volatile," said one dealer.
The benchmark FTSE 100 ended 3.6 points lower at 4,895.7 on Monday, having swung erratically within a 33 point range.
The prospect of higher interest rates also worried investors on Wall Street, where the Dow, down 14 points when London markets closed, ended 4.41 points higher at 8,198.45.
Dealers said the FTSE futures market, responsible for much of Monday's volatility, was likely to continue to drive thin markets.
"I don't get the sense that there's any real selling pressure, but there are a lot of profits around and I think people are going to start to bank them," the dealer said.

Those not prepared to take profits have started to hedge their holdings with index futures and options, he said. That could continue for the next few weeks, if months, and the result will be more volatility, he said.
Yet no one is prepared to call a top to the market ahead of the monetary meeting, dealers said.
"Buyers are still around, but they're not aggressive," another dealer said. "But if anyone sees blood in the water, they'll start selling."
A slew of economic data could influence trading today, though the impact is likely to be limited ahead of the Bank of England's monetary meeting, dealers said.
At 0830 GMT, the UK purchasing managers survey, industrial production and manufacturing output are due for release. At 1000 GMT, the CBI regional trends survey will be published.
Gilts were expected to open steady ahead of the data.

Among individual companies, National Westminster Bank said its first half pre-tax profits from continuing operations rose to 775 million stg from 662 million a year ago. The UK banking group issued an interim dividend of 10.6p per share. The figures generally met analysts' forecasts and dealers said the shares were likely to open steady.
Elsewhere, BAA Plc said its first quarter profits rose to 136.0 million stg, as expected, from 130.0 million stg a year ago.
Later this morning, British Petroleum Plc will post its second quarter results. Profits in the latest quarter were expected near 661.0 million stg, up from 587.0 million stg a year ago.
Among second-liners, Willis Corroon Plc said its interim profits slipped to 60.2 million stg, which was well within industry forecasts, from 68.2 million stg.
Mayflower Corp Plc said its pre-tax profits jumped 58 percent to 16.1 million stg in the first half from 10.2 million stg a year ago.
